title: Natural coefficient-Hom augmentation and its restriction identity
statement: Let phi:R -> B be a homomorphism of commutative ring sheaves on a small site. Let r be restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], rc its extension to unbounded module complexes [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and sigma:R[0] -> rc(B[0]) the map induced by phi. Let epsilon:K -> R[0] and delta:L -> B[0] be augmented R- and B-complexes. Let T be any endofunctor of R-complexes and eta:id -> T any natural transformation. For every u:K -> rc(L) with u;rc(delta)=epsilon;sigma, there are G:C(R) -> C(B), a natural isomorphism c:G;rc ~= Hom_R(rc(L),-) of product internal Hom complexes [def-pur-hom-complex], and a B-linear natural chain map beta:id -> rc;T;G such that, for every B-complex M, rc(beta_M);c_(T rc M);Hom(u,id) equals eta_(rc M);ev_1^(-1);Hom(epsilon,id). Here ev_1 is evaluation at one for Hom_R(R[0],-) [def-weil-pbc-ringed-completion-unit]. No flatness, completeness, quasi-isomorphism or K-injectivity hypothesis is needed.

proof.text: Use the actual coefficient-Hom bifunctor with B-action by precomposition. Its evaluation map attached to e:A -> B and q:r(M) -> N sends a local m to the local R-linear morphism a -> q(e(a)m). This is B-linear under precomposition, restriction-compatible and natural in e, q and m. Extend the separately additive bifunctor to the product Hom-complex functor and normalize its restriction comparison by the product projections.

Fix L. For m in M^n define the p-th product projection of beta_M(m) to be zero for p != 0, and for p=0 use a -> eta^n(delta^0(a)m). The product universal property constructs each degree map. On the p=0 projection the chain-map equation is the chain-map equation for eta. On p=-1 the extra Hom differential term vanishes by delta d_L=0. On all other projections both sides vanish. Thus beta is a B-linear chain map, and naturality of eta gives naturality in M. This works equally for zero complexes and for zero eta.

Restrict beta and precompose with u. On every product projection its value on x is eta(phi(epsilon(x))m)=epsilon(x)eta(m), by the augmentation square and R-linearity of eta. Evaluation-at-one inverse followed by precomposition with epsilon has exactly this formula. Equality of all product projections gives equality of chain maps. For phi=id and L=K=R[0] with identity augmentations this reduces to evaluation at one.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_coefficientHom_augmentation
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    {R B : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (φ : R ⟶ B)
    (K : ringedSiteComplex R) (ε : K ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex R)
    (L : ringedSiteComplex B) (δ : L ⟶ ringedSiteRingComplex B)
    (T : ringedSiteComplex R ⥤ ringedSiteComplex R)
    (η : 𝟭 (ringedSiteComplex R) ⟶ T) :
    let r := SheafOfModules.restrictScalars.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)
    let rc := r.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let σ : ringedSiteRingComplex R ⟶ rc.obj (ringedSiteRingComplex B) :=
      (HomologicalComplex.single _ (.up ℤ) 0).map
          (SheafOfModules.LocalizationCech.unitMap φ) ≫
        (HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex r (.up ℤ) 0).inv.app
          (SheafOfModules.unit ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B))
    ∀ (u : K ⟶ rc.obj L), u ≫ rc.map δ = ε ≫ σ →
      ∃ G : ringedSiteComplex R ⥤ ringedSiteComplex B,
        ∃ c : G ⋙ rc ≅ (homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op (rc.obj L)),
          ∃ β : 𝟭 (ringedSiteComplex B) ⟶ rc ⋙ T ⋙ G,
            ∀ M : ringedSiteComplex B,
              rc.map (β.app M) ≫ c.hom.app (T.obj (rc.obj M)) ≫
                  ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).map u.op).app (T.obj (rc.obj M)) =
                (by
                  change rc.obj M ⟶
                    ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).obj (op K)).obj (T.obj (rc.obj M))
                  exact η.app (rc.obj M) ≫
                    (ringedHomUnitEvaluationIso R (T.obj (rc.obj M))).inv ≫
                    ((homComplexFunctor (R := R)).map ε.op).app (T.obj (rc.obj M)))
